raw.cause: gps_handle() (deadlock fault) calls MsgSend() to nav with MSG_HINT while it is still holding nav's MSG_POSITION message unreplied. nav's only thread is REPLY-blocked on gps inside nav_handle(), so it can never MsgReceive the hint: gps stays SEND-blocked on nav and nav stays REPLY-blocked on gps forever. The contract forbids gps -> nav precisely because gps is a leaf server and any send back up the chain closes a cycle.
raw.qnx_call: MsgSend in gps (gps_handle -> ask(gps_nav, MSG_HINT)) while nav's MSG_POSITION is unreplied
raw.fix_summary: Remove the gps -> nav send. gps must answer MSG_POSITION from its own state and never open a connection to nav. If gps really needs route hints, nav should push them down in its MSG_POSITION request (nav -> gps is allowed), so messages flow in one direction only. Do not just add gps -> nav to the contract: that would legitimise a send cycle that deadlocks.
